entries.claim: `status` can advertise an outstanding dispatchable plan for a phase that `replay-check` refuses to dispatch, because it reads only `p.plans` and never applies replay-check's nonconforming-plan gate.
entries.failure_scenario: Create a phase containing a valid unfinished `PLAN.md` and an invalid plan-shaped file such as `PLAN-x.md`. `derivePhases` supplies the valid plan in `p.plans`, so `status` returns `outstanding: [{ phase: 1, plans: ['PLAN.md'] }]`. But `replay-check --phase 1` calls `listPlanFiles` and fails when `nonconforming` is nonempty, producing no `dispatch_set`. A router using the new outstanding field will send work to replay-check that cannot run, contradicting the claimed shared dispatch set and leaving the phase unroutable.

counter_evidence.note: cmdReplayCheck returns ok({...}) with dispatch_set unconditionally and spreads nonconforming_plans onto that same envelope as an ADDITIVE key (line 54); it never refuses on it. Its only two refusals are fail(bad-args) on a phase-spelling collision (lines 22-25) and fail(no-phase-dir) when listPlanFiles reports missing (lines 28-31), neither of which reads nonconforming. core.mjs:317-322 returns nonconforming beside a populated plans array rather than throwing, so a PLAN-x.md sibling leaves PLAN.md in plans and dispatch_set is derived from it via the same readPlanReports call status uses for outstanding.
